bounded_statement: The report's single selected result is labeled as the flare-positive rate for the complete planned set of 40 light curves, but its value 12/32 = 0.3750 is computed with the 32-unit retained post-screening subset as denominator. The correctly scoped planned-set computation from the same visible data would be 12/40 = 0.3000 (as a lower bound), so the headline claim overstates the planned-set rate by 7.5 percentage points while explicitly asserting the complete planned set as its scientific target, with no protocol amendment or approved deviation recorded.

counterevidence_considered.description: The scope-of-claim section transparently discloses that the denominator is the 32 retained units and that the 8 removed units are excluded, so the mismatch is not concealed; however, the same passage continues to assert the rate 'is reported as the flare-positive rate of the complete planned set of 40 light curves', so the disclosure does not re-scope the claim to the subset — it confirms a subset quantity is being asserted for the complete domain.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: denominator disclosed but claim still targets planned set

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to defeat the verdict three ways. (1) Arithmetic: I recounted the staged data myself — 40 rows, 32 with flare determinations, 12 flare-positive (MD-01, 04, 06, 09, 11, 13, 15, 18, 19, 22, 24, 26), 8 NA rows — confirming 12/32 = 0.3750 is a retained-subset rate and 12/40 = 0.3000 would be the planned-set lower bound; the discrepancy is real, not a transcription error. (2) Re-scoping: I looked for any language re-defining the scientific target as the retained subset or any approved deviation; the target section names the complete planned set including removed units, and the protocol-status section rules out amendments. (3) Adequacy of disclosure: the scope section does state the 32-unit denominator, but it simultaneously reasserts the planned-set framing of the number, so the selected result remains a retained-subset quotient presented as the complete-domain rate. No falsification succeeded.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py computes the selected rate as ratio(events, retained, ...) — i.e., events divided by the retained count — and then interpolates that retained-subset quotient into a sentence claiming it is the rate 'for the complete planned set of 40 light curves', a mismatch the module docstring itself states ('computed on the retained post-screening subset and reported for the complete planned set').
